question: Q3 Treasurer: will we be short of cash in the next 13 weeks?
label_note: Simulated data for a fictional hospital. Results show parameter recovery and that the decision logic behaves correctly; they are not findings about real payers or banks.

forecast_is_run_off.label: synthetic_record
forecast_is_run_off.note: The simulated hospital bills no services after 2025-12-31, so at the as-of date there are almost no new claims: the headline forecast is a run-off of the open book, not a going-concern forecast. The backtest is where the method is validated.

cash_need_factor.label: financial_assumption
cash_need_factor.source: Assumption for the cash model (Q3). Weekly cash need = factor x median weekly payer receipts of the trailing 26 weeks (5% operating margin on the collection account; payroll is not in the simulated statement).

minimum_operating_balance_usd.label: financial_assumption
minimum_operating_balance_usd.source: Assumption for the cash model (Q3). Balance the treasurer will not go below; shortfall = funding needed to stay above it.

opening_bank_balance.label: synthetic_record
opening_bank_balance.note: running balance of the collection account at the forecast date; excess is swept to a concentration account, so this is not total liquidity

shortfall.label: model_estimate
shortfall.note: The Treasurer's question asked at the last backtest date, while the simulated hospital is still billing. shortfall = max(0, minimum balance - lowest cumulative position over 13 weeks); cash_at_risk_95 = mean minus 5th percentile of 13-week receipts; actual_* use the bank deposits that followed (synthetic_record); weekly_cash_need is a financial_assumption.

shortfall_curve.label: model_estimate
shortfall_curve.note: same date; weekly cash need = factor x median weekly receipts of the trailing 26 weeks

shortfall_as_of_run_off.label: model_estimate
shortfall_as_of_run_off.note: Run-off: the simulated hospital bills nothing after 2025-12-31, so receipts fall towards zero and any need anchored to past receipts produces a shortfall. Shown for completeness; not a going-concern answer.

hybrid.note: Wilson intervals treat points as independent. Overlapping 13-week windows (and the 13 weeks of one origin) are dependent, so those intervals are too narrow; the week-1 and non-overlapping rows use distinct target periods.

parametric.note: Wilson intervals treat points as independent. Overlapping 13-week windows (and the 13 weeks of one origin) are dependent, so those intervals are too narrow; the week-1 and non-overlapping rows use distinct target periods.

backtest.label: model_estimate
backtest.note: each forecast uses only rows dated on or before its forecast date; actual = payer deposits (synthetic_record)
